stemMd: Which of the following can be inferred from the excerpt?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The fullers controlled the decisions of the council.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The weavers were indifferent to the bell.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The fullers' work depended on coordination between workshops more than the weavers' work did.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The weavers worked longer hours than the fullers.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The fullers were richer than the wool merchants.

explanationMd:
An inference question asks for a conclusion the text supports without stating it. Look for two facts that can be put side by side.

About the fullers, the excerpt says they "worked in shifts at the river and needed to know when the right to use the water passed from one workshop to the next". About the weavers, it says they "worked at home and had no need to coordinate with anyone". Setting these together supports the choice that the fullers' work depended on coordination between workshops more than the weavers' did.

The others go beyond the text. Hours worked, relative wealth and control of the council are never compared. And the weavers cannot have been indifferent, since they petitioned about the bell.

**Check:** a correct inference is usually modest ("more than", "at least") and can be traced to two named sentences. A sweeping claim about wealth, power or motives that the excerpt never mentions is almost always a trap.

distractorRationale.d: The excerpt says nothing about how long either group worked. It says only that the bell announced the hours the weavers already kept.
distractorRationale.e: The fullers paid half the cost, but the excerpt gives no comparison of wealth. The merchants' opposition was to the expense, and nothing shows they could not afford it.
distractorRationale.a: The fullers made the request and offered to pay half, but the excerpt does not show them directing the council. The council bought the bell only on that condition, and it kept the bell and refused the weavers without any mention of the fullers.
distractorRationale.b: The weavers petitioned about the bell and objected to its being in the council's keeping. That is a strong reaction, not indifference.

accessibilityText: A reading question about the accompanying excerpt on a town bell in Montalbero. It asks which of five statements about the fullers, the weavers, the merchants and the council can be inferred from the text. None uses notation or figures.

provenance.notes: Original item written against an original excerpt authored alongside it. The answer is deducible from the excerpt alone; no outside knowledge is needed or used.

review.author: polito-til-wave6-til-i-reading-logic-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: Fullers worked in shifts and needed to know when water rights passed between workshops, while the weavers 'had no need to coordinate with anyone'. That supports C. A overreaches, since the council refused the weavers without the fullers deciding anything, and the fullers had to pay half the cost. B is contradicted by the weavers' petition. D and E are unsupported. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave6-tili-reading-logic-run6) reached the same answer: Fullers worked in shifts and needed to know when water rights passed between workshops. Weavers 'had no need to coordinate with anyone'. So C follows. B contradicts the weavers' petition. A, D and E are unsupported; the council refused a request, and the merchants opposed the purchase at first.]

review.notes: Inference item built on a comparison of two stated facts (fullers coordinate, weavers do not). Each distractor asserts a comparison or claim of which the excerpt gives no evidence, or which it contradicts. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key.
